name: phosphoinositide-3-kinase regulatory subunit 2
pathways: positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

function.text: PIK3R2 encodes phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase regulatory subunit beta. Annotated molecular activities include 1-phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase regulator activity and protein heterodimerization activity. It participates in phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B signal transduction and positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to overgrowth syndrome and/or cerebral malformations due to abnormalities in MTOR pathway genes (autosomal dominant); megalencephaly-polymicrogyria-polydactyly-hydrocephalus syndrome 1 (autosomal dominant).

function.text: PIK3R2 encodes phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase regulatory subunit beta. Based in part on similarity, PIP3 plays a key role by recruiting PH domain-containing proteins to the membrane, including AKT1 and PDPK1, activating signaling cascades involved in cell growth, survival, proliferation, motility and morphology. It binds to activated (phosphorylated) protein-tyrosine kinases, through its SH2 domain, and acts as an adapter, mediating the association of the p110 catalytic unit to the plasma membrane.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with overgrowth syndrome and/or cerebral malformations due to abnormalities in MTOR pathway genes (autosomal dominant); megalencephaly-polymicrogyria-polydactyly-hydrocephalus syndrome 1 (autosomal dominant).
